# E158 -- Ogden Museum

## Metadata
- **Organization:** Ogden Museum of Southern Art
- **Year:** 2016
- **Sector:** Museum / Cultural
- **Pages:** 30
- **Design Agency:** Not credited (appears in-house)
- **Format Quality:** Functional but modest; InDesign CC 2015 output, letter-size landscape PDF

## Brand Strategy
Mission-driven: broaden knowledge, understanding, and appreciation of visual arts and culture of the American South. Brand philosophy centers on simplicity, modernity, and cleanliness -- intended to enhance rather than distract from exhibitions and programming. Emphasizes creating a welcoming environment that "invites ALL." No formal brand pillars or positioning framework articulated beyond the mission statement.

## Logo
- Distinctive "O" mark (square, 6p0 x 6p0) paired with wordmark
- Multiple layout variants: stacked, stacked-right, centered
- Clear space: 1p0 between logo and text (vertical and horizontal)
- Logo text: Helvetica Regular, all caps, 16pt, tracking 100, leading 19.2pt
- Color hierarchy: Red logo with white O preferred (on white background); black or white alternatives for contrast situations
- Transparent O variant allows background imagery to show through (requires deputy director approval)
- Detailed incorrect-usage examples provided (no text on O, no tilting, "of" must stay on same line as "southern art")
- Departmental sub-brands may use colors other than red

## Typography
Three-tier type system:
- **Primary:** Helvetica (Light through Bold Oblique) -- used as header font and with Ogden Museum name mentions
- **Secondary:** Avenir (Light through Heavy Oblique) -- body copy, light weight preferred; other weights as secondary elements
- **Tertiary:** Bebas Neue -- display font only
- Rule: no more than two font combinations per item (with exceptions)
- Departmental sub-brands may introduce one additional typeface

## Color
Minimal palette, red-dominant:
- **Primary:** PMS 485 (CMYK 0/100/100/0, HEX #ec1c24) -- must appear in some form on all corporate branding
- **White:** PMS White (#ffffff)
- **Light Grey:** PMS Cool Grey 2 (CMYK 0/0/0/20, #d1d2d4)
- **Mid Grey:** PMS 423 (CMYK 0/0/0/50, #939597)
- **Black:** PMS 426 (CMYK 0/0/0/100, #000000)
- Philosophy: "less is more" -- minimalist use of red to avoid overpowering the logo

## Graphics
Minimal graphic system. The "O" mark itself serves as the primary graphic device, occasionally used with image/pattern fills inside. Sparse use of triple-slash (///) as a typographic accent in exhibition materials. Exhibition banners use bold typographic treatments with generous tracking and all-caps display.

## Photography
No formal photography guidelines documented. Exhibition collateral relies on artwork imagery (paintings, photographs from collections). Photography is treated as content rather than brand asset.

## Applications
Extensive application coverage (pages 10-30):
- Exhibition display collateral (banners, sandwich boards)
- Museum print collateral (invitations, programs, postcards)
- Digital blasts (email templates)
- Departmental branding (sub-brands for different museum programs)
- Additional elements
- Exhibition materials show consistent layout patterns: artwork image, exhibition title in display type, dates with /// prefix notation

## Tone of Voice
Not formally documented as a section. Intro text suggests approachable, inclusive, culturally proud tone. Language emphasizes openness ("invites ALL") and the significance of Southern art's global impact.

## Outliers
- The "O" as a container/window device (allowing imagery inside) is a distinctive brand mechanic not always seen in museum guidelines
- Departmental sub-branding system allowing color and typeface deviations is notably flexible for a brand guide
- Triple-slash (///) notation as a consistent typographic detail in exhibition materials
- No digital/web-specific guidelines despite 30 pages

## Quality Score
**2.5 / 5** -- Covers logo, color, and typography basics adequately with clear do/don't examples. Heavy emphasis on application templates (exhibitions, print) which is practical but at the expense of strategic depth. Lacks photography direction, tone of voice documentation, digital guidelines, and any brand narrative beyond the mission statement. Production quality is functional rather than polished.
